info.title: Tronicare Users API
info.description: Source-derived HTTP contract for the users api process. Mutation routes return 503 while mutations are disabled or write authority is unavailable. JSON records preserve legacy member spelling and signed 64-bit integer values. Unknown JSON members are ignored, but duplicate keys, non-finite numbers and invalid UTF-8 are rejected. Request bodies are limited to 1,048,576 bytes. This offline document does not enable a runtime /openapi.json or interactive docs endpoint.

servers.description: The selected users api listener; configure the deployment base URL.

get.description: Check process liveness.
Returns 200 when ready and 503 when unavailable. API dependency checks time out after five seconds.

503.description: Process or dependencies are not ready.

get.description: Requires entity users right r. Returns a raw array ordered by primary key. More than 10,000 candidate rows returns 503. Ordinary callers are restricted to their organization; userlog records are scoped through their owning user. Asset matching is delegated to the Assets reader. Deleted records may remain visible to authorized readers.  The shared handler also accepts the implicit entity_id query parameter; GET then returns one record and skips collection filters. Authentication and rights are checked against current Users database state. Deleted users and expired sessions are rejected. For every noninternal caller, m_sHash, m_sCode, m_sToken and m_sOldLogin are projected as empty strings in successful responses; wire member names are preserved.

parameters.name: entity_id
parameters.description: Implicit FastAPI query argument from the shared handler. If supplied to GET, this reads one record instead of listing; collection filters are ignored. POST validates this value but still creates a new record with a generated ID. Repeated entity_id values use the last value. Signed 64-bit integer.

parameters.name: idorganization
parameters.description: Filter by organization. Signed 64-bit decimal integer; empty means omitted. Repeated values are rejected. The numeric value must be between -9223372036854775808 and 9223372036854775807.

parameters.name: idusergroup
parameters.description: Filter by usergroup. Signed 64-bit decimal integer; empty means omitted. Repeated values are rejected. The numeric value must be between -9223372036854775808 and 9223372036854775807.

parameters.name: idasset
parameters.description: Filter by asset. Signed 64-bit decimal integer; empty means omitted. Repeated values are rejected. The numeric value must be between -9223372036854775808 and 9223372036854775807.

post.description: Requires entity users right c. Requires enabled mutations and authoritative write state. Returns the created record with HTTP 200 and a generated primary key.  The shared handler also accepts the implicit entity_id query parameter; GET then returns one record and skips collection filters. Authentication and rights are checked against current Users database state. Deleted users and expired sessions are rejected. Ordinary callers are restricted to their organization, including when entity_id selects a single item. Persisted one-time-password sessions cannot use CRUD mutations. Authorization failures occur before record mutation and audit creation. Ordinary callers may create or modify only a non-admin account in their organization whose valid role level is strictly lower than theirs. PUT and DELETE protect the persisted target even when role and admin members are omitted; effective submitted role and organization are checked as well. Noninternal CRUD callers, including platform administrators, cannot supply credential members m_sHash, m_sCode, m_sToken, m_sOldLogin, m_bCodeUsed or m_dhCodeExpired; use the dedicated password/signup/recovery flows. For every noninternal caller, m_sHash, m_sCode, m_sToken and m_sOldLogin are projected as empty strings in successful responses; wire member names are preserved.

requestBody.description: A JSON object, at most 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes. Empty object is accepted.

get.summary: Log in and create a session
get.description: Creates a one-hour session. Trims login and password; uppercases the password. Client version 1.0 uses the legacy server-side password digest transformation; other clients provide the digest or one-time code. Failed login returns HTTP 200 with status=false and token="null". This legacy GET route mutates state and requires enabled mutations and authoritative write state; disabled mutations return 503 before credential processing. This admin route allows an absent or empty Token; malformed or duplicate Token headers still return 401. Query values cannot contain NUL or be repeated. Deleted accounts cannot log in. Session one-time-password state is persisted in PostgreSQL; database expiration is enforced independently of worker cache cleanup.

401.description: Authentication failed or invalid Token header.

409.description: Request conflicts with the current state.

503.description: Required dependency unavailable, timeout, disabled mutations or unavailable write authority.
